headline: Homebuilders Lead a Tentative Advance as Breadth Stays Split
body_html:
Midday Monday, the market is threading a narrow path higher, with advancing issues just barely edging out decliners — 262 up against 282 down across the 549-name universe. The session's dominant theme is geopolitical risk meeting macro anticipation: Strait of Hormuz uncertainty is keeping energy traders on edge, while an upcoming U.S. inflation print has investors reluctant to commit too aggressively in either direction.

Sector leadership is telling. Homebuilders pace the tape with a gain of 1.57%, suggesting rate-sensitive buyers see something they like — or at least less to fear — heading into the data. Energy is next at 0.88%, supported by oil prices that have inched upward as Iran signals its Hormuz conditions are far from simple. Semiconductors are holding a modest 0.64% advance. On the other side, software is the session's clearest laggard, off 0.73%, and healthcare is a touch softer as well.

The standout mover of the morning is N-able, the IT-management software firm, which has plunged roughly 35% and is drawing most of the session's attention. Into the close, watch whether software weakness broadens and whether the Hormuz headline flow shifts oil — and energy equities — in either direction.

briefs.headline: N-able Collapse Dominates Software Tape
briefs.body: Shares of N-able have cratered nearly 35% midday Monday, making it by far the most dramatic single-name move in the session. The IT-management software name is pulling outsized attention and weighing on broader software sentiment, which sits at the bottom of the sector ledger at minus 0.73%.

briefs.headline: Covista Surges More Than 13% on Heavy Volume
briefs.body: Covista, the consumer-education company formerly known as Adtalem, has rocketed 13.46% intraday, placing it atop the session's gainers board. The move stands in sharp contrast to sector-peer Universal Technical Institute, which is simultaneously sliding nearly 5%, underscoring a divergence within the education space.

briefs.headline: Iran's Hormuz Stance Keeps Oil Markets Guarded
briefs.body: Tehran has linked any reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to a list of concessions from Washington, tempering earlier optimism that a swift resolution was at hand. Oil prices have edged higher on the cautious tone, supporting Energy's 0.88% sector gain while keeping traders alert to any fresh headline that could quickly reprice the commodity.

briefs.headline: Gold Retreats Slightly Ahead of U.S. Inflation Data
briefs.body: Bullion has slipped a touch from a seven-week high as markets brace for an upcoming U.S. consumer-price reading. The inflation data is expected to set the near-term tone for rate expectations, and gold's modest pullback reflects some positioning caution rather than a decisive shift in sentiment.

briefs.headline: Marvell Paces Semiconductor Sector Recovery
briefs.body: Marvell Technology has added 4.43% midday, helping anchor the Semiconductors sector to a 0.64% advance and providing one of the session's cleaner stories of fundamental demand for chip-adjacent infrastructure. The gain comes as global equity markets register a mild upward tick despite unresolved geopolitical pressures.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Assert Themselves as Rate-Sensitive Leaders
briefs.body: The Homebuilders group is outpacing every other sector Monday with a gain of 1.57%, suggesting the market is pricing in some degree of relief on the interest-rate outlook ahead of the inflation print. The move is notable given the otherwise mixed breadth across the broader universe.
